sections.html:
Puyallup is a Pierce County city on the Puyallup River, roughly 10 miles from Tacoma and 35 miles from Seattle. Population stands at 42,682 as of July 1, 2025, a 0.7% dip from the April 2020 estimates base. Home values run above $550,000, and many buyers drive to Tacoma, Seattle or other job centers, so commute time shapes offers.

Many sellers get caught by one detail. A Puyallup mailing address can sit in unincorporated territory such as South Hill. Confirm that your parcel is within city limits, because that decides your permit office, zoning code and utility rules. The county bills property tax in both cases.

Use these figures as a rough frame when you talk price with a buyer or agent. They describe the whole city, not your street.

Housing measurePuyallup city, 2020 to 2024
Owner-occupied housing unit rate52.1%
Median value of owner-occupied homes$551,800
Median gross rent$1,812
Households16,570
Persons per household2.53
Mean travel time to work31.4 minutes
Median household income$97,826

The median is an average across every owner-occupied home, old and new. A house that has been updated can price well above it, and one with deferred repairs can price below it.

sections.h2: Can I build a cottage or add a unit in the lahar zone?
sections.html:
Downtown Puyallup and nearby neighborhoods lie within a hazard zone for lahars, which are mudflows that a moderate or large Mount Rainier eruption could send down the Puyallup Valley. City rules respond to that risk. Under Puyallup Municipal Code 20.20.010(11)(L), accessory dwelling units are prohibited in the lahar exclusion area, with an exception for land within a half mile of the base of the surrounding elevation of the valley floor.

The city's September 2025 tip sheet lists what owners in that area can still do:

  • Build an addition or remodel that has an internal doorway and is not fully fire-wall separated from the main home.
  • Rent that added space to family or, if not family, to no more than one person.
  • Keep a guest house in a detached building, as long as it has no independent cooking facilities and no one lives there full time, with limited exceptions for family and employees.

If your house has a converted garage, a basement apartment or a backyard cottage, ask the Planning Division how the city treats it before you list. An unpermitted second unit can complicate a sale. Call 253-864-4165, option 3, or email Planning@PuyallupWA.gov.

Permit questions go to the Permit Center on the second floor of City Hall, 333 South Meridian. The counter is staffed from 9 a.m. to 3 p.m., and the main number is 253-864-4165. Before you take an offer, call about any building permit still open on the house. Unfinished permits tend to turn up in a buyer's inspection or at title review, and closing one out is simpler while the deadline is yours.

Have the street address ready, plus the permit number and contractor paperwork if you kept them. Staff can pull the file and tell you which inspection is missing.

Washington charges the seller a graduated state excise tax on the price (RCW 82.45.080). The county adds a local share, and the Pierce County Assessor-Treasurer can quote the combined figure for your address. Under the schedule that runs through December 31, 2026, the first tier is 1.1% up to $525,000, then 1.28% to $1,525,000, then 2.75% to $3,025,000, and 3% on anything higher.

Sales beginning January 1, 2027 use higher breakpoints: $551,000, $1,551,000 and $3,051,000. Puyallup's median home value of $551,800 lands almost exactly on the first of those, which makes a closing date near year end something to raise with your escrow officer.

Tax timing follows the day the deed is notarized, not the day it is recorded. The deed, the affidavit and the payment all go to the county treasurer. If you overpay, you have four years from the sale to ask for a refund, and the request is made by whoever paid.

Pierce County splits the annual bill into two installments, April 30 and October 31. A weekend October 31 pushes the second installment to the next Monday. Small bills of $50 or less are due once, by April 30.

Miss the April deadline on a residential parcel of one to four units, and interest runs at 0.75% a month on the whole year's tax from May 1 (tax years 2023 and later). Paying the first half with interest by October 31 is still allowed. If a late balance exists at closing, the closing officer can pay it out of your proceeds.

The county revalues every property at 100% of market value each year and sends someone to look at each parcel roughly every six years. If you think the value is wrong, file with the Board of Equalization by July 1 of the assessment year, or within 60 days after a value change notice if that is later. The board hears arguments about market value only. The size of the tax bill is not up for debate.

sections.h2: If you have a tax deferral
sections.html:
Older owners and owners with disabilities can defer property tax under RCW 84.38. The state covers the bill, and what it paid becomes a lien that comes due, with interest, once the property changes hands. A sale triggers that repayment, so order a payoff figure early and hand it to the title company before the closing numbers are drawn up.

Visit the Assessor-Treasurer at 2401 South 35th Street, Room 142, in Tacoma, or call 253-798-6111.

sections.h2: Ways to sell and how closing works
sections.html:
You can list with an agent, sell on your own, or take an as-is offer from a cash buyer. Whichever way you go, the sale ends with a deed, an excise tax affidavit and a tax proration.

  • Listing: the broadest set of buyers, at the price of showings and loan approvals.
  • As-is cash offer: a fit for deferred repairs, an unpermitted unit or a conversion inside the lahar zone.
  • With any buyer, pin down what the price covers, who pays the excise tax, and when the deed will be notarized.

In order, a closing runs like this. Price and date are agreed, escrow opens at a title company, and the buyer examines title and the house. Payoffs for loans or a deferral are requested, you sign the deed before a notary, and the affidavit and tax payment go to the county. Property tax is split between you and the buyer by closing date, then funds are released once the deed is recorded.

Pull together your deed, a payoff statement, permit records and the newest tax bill before talking to anyone. A cash purchase has no appraisal and no lender underwriting, which leaves title work and your own schedule as the only clocks.

faqs.q: Can I build a backyard cottage in Puyallup's lahar zone?
faqs.a: No. Puyallup Municipal Code 20.20.010(11)(L) prohibits accessory dwelling units in the lahar exclusion area, with an exception near the edge of the valley floor. A guest house with no independent cooking, not lived in full time, may be allowed.

faqs.q: When is the second half of Pierce County property tax due?
faqs.a: Pierce County sets October 31, shifted to the next Monday if it falls on a weekend. The first installment is due April 30, and bills of $50 or less are paid once, by that date.

faqs.q: How does the excise tax change in 2027?
faqs.a: Sales through December 31, 2026 use state breakpoints of $525,000, $1,525,000 and $3,025,000. Sales beginning January 1, 2027 use $551,000, $1,551,000 and $3,051,000. The notarized deed date picks the schedule.

faqs.q: Does a South Hill address mean my house is in the city of Puyallup?
faqs.a: Not always. Puyallup mailing addresses cover adjacent unincorporated areas such as South Hill. Check your parcel with the city Planning Division or the county to confirm which rules apply.

faqs.q: What happens to a senior property tax deferral when I sell?
faqs.a: The state's payment becomes a lien, due with interest when the house changes hands. Ask the Pierce County Assessor-Treasurer for a payoff figure ahead of closing.
